subsystems.name: Sensing front end
subsystems.role: measures what the body actually needs, continuously.

subsystems.name: Fluid handling
subsystems.role: moves microlitre volumes of sample and reagents without clogging or leaking.

subsystems.name: Synthesis reactor
subsystems.role: converts a stored precursor into the target molecule.

subsystems.name: Purification and dosing
subsystems.role: makes sure what is delivered is the right molecule, in the right amount, at the right time.

subsystems.name: Control and power
subsystems.role: runs the closed loop and keeps the device alive on a small battery.
parts: encrypted radio link to a phone

buildSteps.title: Pick a target you can actually make
buildSteps.detail: Only molecules reachable in one or two enzymatic or catalytic steps from a stable, stored precursor are candidates. Most vitamins and most peptide hormones need many steps and are not realistic first targets. Skin already makes vitamin D3 photochemically from a precursor, which is the closest natural precedent for on-body synthesis.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensing layer
buildSteps.detail: Microneedle arrays that reach interstitial fluid are fabricated, coated with selective chemistries, and calibrated against blood samples. Multiple analytes on one patch is the hard part.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the fluidic cartridge
buildSteps.detail: Channels, valves and pumps are moulded or etched in polymer and bonded into a sealed, sterile, replaceable card holding the precursor and reagents.

buildSteps.title: Immobilise the catalyst
buildSteps.detail: Enzymes or catalysts are fixed onto beads or a membrane inside the reactor so they are not consumed and do not enter the body. Stability over days at skin temperature must be demonstrated.

buildSteps.title: Add separation and dosing
buildSteps.detail: A capture or membrane step removes by-products, then an in-line sensor verifies the product before it passes through microneedles into the skin.

buildSteps.title: Write the closed loop
buildSteps.detail: Control software reads the sensor, predicts the need, and commands a dose — the same control problem already solved for automated insulin delivery, but with synthesis in the loop instead of a reservoir.

buildSteps.title: Engineer fail-safes
buildSteps.detail: Redundant measurement, a watchdog that stops the reactor, limits on total daily dose, and a way for a clinician to see and override every action.

buildSteps.title: Validate clinically
buildSteps.detail: Bench accuracy, animal studies, then tightly monitored human trials measuring whether the loop actually improves outcomes rather than just producing plausible numbers.

prerequisites.why: continuous glucose monitors prove the principle for one analyte; reliable, calibration-free sensing of hormones and vitamins is not there yet.
commercially available hybrid closed-loop insulin systems show automated dosing works, but they deliver a pre-made drug from a reservoir — they do not synthesise it.
continuous synthesis on a chip is routine in laboratories, but doing it in a sealed wearable for days is unproven.
biological catalysts must survive body temperature and constant flow for a week or more without losing activity.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory route for an on-body reactor
prerequisites.why: no framework exists for a device that manufactures a regulated drug inside a patient.

pathway.milestone: wearable multi-analyte sensing in research and early products, alongside reservoir-based closed-loop insulin delivery
pathway.unlocks: proof that a body-worn closed loop can be safe and useful.

pathway.milestone: a wearable that synthesises one simple molecule from a stored precursor, verified by an independent sensor
pathway.unlocks: the core feasibility question — can on-body chemistry be trusted?

pathway.milestone: clinician-supervised trials in a narrow, well-monitored deficiency condition
pathway.unlocks: evidence for benefit and a regulatory precedent.

pathway.milestone: multi-molecule devices with validated safety layers
pathway.unlocks: preventative use at scale — only if the chemistry, stability and oversight problems are all solved together.
